title: Certified Angus Beef
about: The Certified Angus Beef brand began in Ohio in 1978. Harold Etling, an Angus breeder from Marshallville, wrote to the American Angus Association after one disappointing steak too many. Mick Colvin then built the program from his home in West Salem. Ranchers worked with Dr. Bob VanStavern, a meat scientist at The Ohio State University, to set the standards, and the first pound sold in Columbus that October.

The brand owns no cattle and no farms. It is a not-for-profit subsidiary of the American Angus Association, governed by Angus ranchers. Black-hided cattle qualify only if the beef passes ten separate standards, among them modest or higher marbling with a fine texture, an age under thirty months and a limit on carcass size. Nearly one in four U.S. carcasses earns the label. The brand has been based in Wooster since 1994, and its Culinary Center trains chefs and butchers in a working meat lab.
Eden’s Ember Roasted NY Strip is Certified Angus Beef, cooked over the hearth.
